events.title: India’s high-speed rail journey
events.description: From the foundation ceremony to civil works, train procurement and 2026 testing updates on the Mumbai–Ahmedabad corridor.
events.tagline: An ambitious connection. Years in the making.
events.imageAlt: ThreadNews illustration of a high-speed train and a schematic Mumbai–Ahmedabad route, not to scale
events.limitation: Public preview: the first 10 selected milestones, from 2017-09-14 through 2026-09-25. Later chronology may be available through the signed-in archive.
events.context: Civil construction, track installation, electrical and signalling systems, rolling-stock manufacture and safety validation are separate workstreams. A completed viaduct or awarded train contract does not mean a line is ready for passengers.
events.watch: Look for dated project measurements, delivered trains, test results and regulatory approvals. Keep ministerial targets separate from demonstrated readiness.
events.keywords: Mumbai Ahmedabad bullet train rail railway Gujarat Maharashtra India NHSRCL transport

events.title: The Strait of Hormuz, under pressure
events.shortTitle: Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz
events.description: Vessel incidents, shipping disruption and diplomacy around the Strait of Hormuz, with official records beside reported claims.
events.tagline: A narrow passage. A worldwide ripple.
events.imageAlt: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz between Iran and Oman, December 2020
events.imageCredit: MODIS / NASA GSFC · public domain · December 2020
events.limitation: Public preview: the first 10 selected milestones, from 2019-06-13 through 2026-09-12. Later chronology may be available through the signed-in archive.
events.context: Hormuz links Gulf producers to global shipping. Its recent history includes vessel seizures, attacks, disruption during the 2026 war and competing negotiating proposals. A passage can carry some traffic while remaining dangerous and heavily restricted.
events.watch: Check the date, vessel identity and source of each incident. Proposals do not establish reopening, and military claims do not independently establish responsibility or a mine as the cause. Singapore’s October flag-state record identifies unknown projectiles.
events.keywords: Hormuz Iran oil tanker shipping Gulf Oman energy maritime strait crisis

milestones.summary: Front Altair and Kokuka Courageous were damaged in the Sea of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz.

sources.title: IMO Council condemns tanker attacks in Strait of Hormuz and Sea of Oman

milestones.note: The event date predates the IMO release. This entry does not establish responsibility for the attacks.

milestones.title: Iran seizes the Stena Impero tanker
milestones.summary: The UK government said Iranian forces intercepted the British-flagged tanker while it was passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

milestones.summary: The US and Iran separately announced plans to send delegations to Qatar, while disagreeing about whether direct talks had been agreed.

milestones.summary: AP reported an Iranian official’s plan for an exclusion zone near Hormuz.

sources.title: Iran-Oman understanding does not provide for immediate reopening of Strait of Hormuz, Tasnim reports

events.title: Russia’s war in Ukraine
events.description: Military, humanitarian and diplomatic turning points in Russia’s war in Ukraine, with closer tracking of recent developments.
events.imageAlt: Illustrative view of Kyiv’s riverfront and bridges across the Dnipro, September 2008
events.imageCredit: Dmitry A. Mottl / Wikimedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · September 2008
events.limitation: Public preview: the first 10 selected milestones, from 2014-03-27 through 2026-09-05. Later chronology may be available through the signed-in archive.
events.context: Russia’s full-scale invasion followed years of conflict after 2014. Military operations, humanitarian arrangements, sanctions and peace initiatives have evolved separately; a local truce or a negotiating announcement does not establish a nationwide ceasefire.
events.watch: Distinguish signed decisions from implementation, casualty reports from final counts, and an announced meeting from an agreed settlement. Official records identify an institution’s position, not independent confirmation of all underlying claims.
events.keywords: Russia Ukraine war invasion Kyiv Europe grain Black Sea UN conflict diplomacy

events.title: Artemis I: to the Moon and back
events.description: The first integrated flight of NASA’s SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft, followed from launch to Pacific splashdown.
events.tagline: One spacecraft. A journey into deep space.
events.imageAlt: NASA’s Artemis I rocket rising from its launch pad at night on 16 November 2022
events.imageCredit: NASA / Joel Kowsky · public domain · November 2022
events.limitation: A completed 2022 mission timeline from NASA’s retrospective. This does not cover later Artemis missions, current programme schedules or independent assessments.
events.context: Artemis I was uncrewed. Its purpose was to test the integrated rocket and spacecraft before later crewed flights. This timeline covers that test mission alone.
events.watch: NASA is both the mission operator and the source. These are official mission records, not independent programme evaluations.

events.title: Azini hijacking and rescue off Somalia
events.description: The reported seizure of the Iranian fishing vessel Azini and the Indian Navy operation that freed its crew, with conflicting reported crew totals kept visible.
events.tagline: Track the incident, the rescue and what remains unclear.
events.imageAlt: ThreadNews illustration of a fishing vessel and rescue route at sea; not a photograph or navigational map
events.keywords: Azini Somalia piracy hijacking Indian Navy Iranian fishing vessel crew maritime security Gulf of Aden
events.limitation: Two selected milestones from the reported seizure through the 3 November rescue announcement. The crew count differs between an earlier local account and India’s official rescue statement; the discrepancy is unresolved.
events.context: A reported hijacking is distinct from a confirmed piracy attribution by a court or international body. The Indian government’s release establishes its own rescue account; it does not explain why an earlier local report gave a different crew count.
events.watch: Look for an independently reconciled crew list, statements from the vessel owner and crew, and any prosecution or maritime-security inquiry.

milestones.title: Armed pirates seize the Azini off Somalia
milestones.summary: AP reported that armed pirates seized the Iranian fishing vessel off Somalia. A local Puntland official cited 23 people aboard; the later Indian rescue statement reported 20 crew.

milestones.note: The initial count of 23 came from a local official. India’s later statement says 20 people were rescued; no linked source reconciles the figures.

milestones.title: India says Navy freed the vessel and rescued 20 crew
milestones.summary: India’s Defence Ministry said an operation lasting more than 48 hours freed the Azini and its 20 crew without injuries. AP reported the rescue and earlier local count; the difference remains unexplained.

sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Defence
sources.title: Indian Navy successfully rescues hijacked fishing vessel Azini off the coast of Somalia

sources.type: Reporting on the rescue and Ministry of Defence account
sources.title: Indian navy rescues 20 crew from Iranian fishing boat hijacked off Somalia

events.title: Air India AI171: the crash and investigation
events.description: Six significant developments in the Ahmedabad crash and the publicly documented investigation, with early reports separated from later records.
events.tagline: Following the evidence, without assigning blame.
events.imageAlt: ThreadNews illustration of an aircraft and dated investigation records; not a photograph of the crash
events.keywords: Air India AI171 flight 171 Ahmedabad Boeing 787 crash AAIB investigation pilots fuel switches safety
events.limitation: Six event milestones through 28 July 2026. AAIB’s public index was checked again on 4 November: the checked page still lists the June 2026 interim statement, and no public AI171 final report was located. This does not establish whether a confidential draft exists.
events.context: A preliminary report records evidence and can change. Fuel-switch transitions alone do not establish who acted, why, or the final cause. Public records reviewed here do not support assigning blame to either pilot.
events.watch: A published AAIB final report and its safety findings would change this account. Confidential court drafts, projected deadlines and unnamed-source allegations are not a public final determination.

milestones.title: Flight AI171 crashes shortly after take-off
milestones.summary: The London-bound Boeing 787 crashed in Ahmedabad. Air India confirmed 241 onboard deaths and one surviving passenger as early reports evolved.

sources.title: Airline confirms one survivor after Ahmedabad crash
Initial report of the Ahmedabad crash

milestones.note: Early ground-fatality totals were provisional. The later AAIB table records 260 deaths in total; do not retain early estimates as the settled count.

milestones.title: Investigators download the front recorder’s data
milestones.summary: The aviation ministry said the front recorder’s memory was accessed and downloaded at AAIB’s Delhi laboratory, enabling voice and flight-data analysis.

sources.title: Recorder recovery and data-extraction status

milestones.note: The ministry’s statement was published on 26 June and dates the successful download to 25 June. Recorder recovery and a cause determination are different steps.

milestones.title: Preliminary report establishes a factual baseline
milestones.summary: AAIB recorded 260 fatalities: 241 onboard and 19 on the ground. Recorder data showed both fuel switches changing to cutoff, then back to run.

sources.title: AI171 preliminary accident report

milestones.note: The preliminary report does not identify who moved the switches or why, establish a final cause, or assign blame. The 15-page report was read; its fatality table was checked visually.

milestones.title: AAIB rejects claims that the probe is finalised
milestones.summary: AAIB described reports that its investigation had been finalised as incorrect and speculative, saying work remained ongoing and conclusions would follow a final report.

sources.publisher: AAIB / Ministry of Civil Aviation / PIB
sources.title: AAIB says investigation remains ongoing

milestones.note: This is an official clarification at that date. It does not establish whether a later draft was submitted confidentially.

milestones.title: Anniversary statement says integrated analysis continues
milestones.summary: AAIB said aircraft systems, recorders, engine components, maintenance and human factors remained under examination; a final report required investigation and international consultation.

sources.publisher: AAIB / Ministry of Civil Aviation / PIB
sources.title: AI171 investigation progress statement

milestones.note: The authority reiterated that safety investigations aim to prevent accidents, not apportion blame or liability.

milestones.title: Ministry tells Rajya Sabha AI171 investigation remains in progress
milestones.summary: In a written answer to Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question 806, the Civil Aviation Ministry said the AI171 investigation was ongoing, all probable causes and contributing factors were being investigated, and the final report would be published after the investigation. It gave no predictable completion date. The answer also reported no abnormality in an OEM examination of a fuel-control-switch locking mechanism after a separate February 2026 grounding, while inspection of the complete Thrust Control Module remained underway; that test is not a finding on AI171's cause.

sources.publisher: Government of India, Ministry of Civil Aviation / Rajya Sabha
sources.title: Unstarred Question No. 806: Delay in publication of AAIB final report on AI-171 crash

milestones.note: The answer makes no finding about pilot culpability or exoneration. Its fuel-control-switch test concerns airworthiness testing following a separate February 2026 grounding; it must not be presented as a causal finding for AI171. The latest AAIB status statement located in this review is its 12 June 2026 interim statement, which said integrated analysis and any necessary specialist examinations were continuing.

milestones.title: Court hears an October target for a draft report
milestones.summary: PTI reported that the government told the Supreme Court a draft final report was expected in early October and would be submitted under seal.

sources.title: Court hears forecast for an AI171 draft report

milestones.note: A forecast for a confidential draft is not publication of a final investigation report. No conclusion about pilot intent or blame follows from this procedural update.

statusCheck.observation: AAIB’s public What’s New page was reviewed on 4 November 2026. It listed the June 2026 interim statement; the preliminary VT-ANB report was also checked. A public AI171 final report was not located in these records. This status check is not a new accident development and does not establish whether a confidential draft was filed in court.

Preliminary Report VT-ANB

events.title: Cyclone Murasu in Andhra Pradesh
events.description: The storm’s formation, landfall near Ongole, weakening and reported impacts, with IMD forecasts separated from casualty reports.
events.tagline: Follow the official storm bulletins and the reported impact.
events.imageAlt: ThreadNews illustration of a coastal storm track; not a satellite image or local scene photograph
events.keywords: Cyclone Murasu Andhra Pradesh Ongole IMD landfall storm surge flooding Prakasam Nellore Bapatla
events.limitation: Five selected developments from the IMD’s storm classification through the 4 November post-landfall update. Casualty and damage reporting was still developing; this is not a final loss assessment.
events.context: IMD bulletins describe the storm’s classification and forecast track. Local authorities and reporters describe effects on communities. Forecast wind speeds, observed landfall conditions, casualties and crop losses are different measures and may be revised.
events.watch: Check each IMD bulletin’s issue time, the storm’s classification at that time, district-level rainfall and river alerts, evacuation status, and subsequent government damage assessments.
